findings.title: Device is cached before the limit check, so a rejected device is later let in
findings.body: tagDeviceUI stores the device key in localCache (line 87) before CreateOrUpdateDevice runs. When the limit is reached, CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached and the device is not tagged, but the key stays cached. For the next ~29 minutes, every request from that device hits the cache hit at line 83 and returns nil, so Authenticate succeeds without the device ever being counted. The first rejection is effectively followed by a bypass of the limit. The cache key should only be set after a successful tag, or removed on error.

findings.title: Device limit check is a non-atomic count followed by insert
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts devices (line 110) and then separately inserts or updates (lines 115-118 and below). Concurrent first-time requests from distinct devices can all read a count below the limit and all insert, so the number of devices can exceed deviceLimit. A correct enforcement needs a single atomic statement or a transaction/lock, and the race should be acknowledged or tested if it is not fixed.

findings.title: rowsAffected == 0 is treated as limit reached, which misfires on MySQL
findings.body: updateDevice treats zero affected rows as ErrDeviceLimitReached. On MySQL, the default driver behaviour reports only changed rows, so an UPDATE that rewrites identical client_ip and user_agent values (common for a returning device) reports 0 rows and is wrongly rejected as if the limit were reached. Also, a device whose updated_at is older than the 30-day window matches nothing and is rejected, even though it already exists and should be updated. The error conflates 'row not found in window' with 'limit reached'.

findings.title: Device tagging is now synchronous on every anonymous authentication
findings.body: The previous implementation ran TagDevice in a goroutine with a 2-minute timeout. It now runs inline on the request path. For any device not in the local cache, each request performs a COUNT over the 30-day window and then a write, so database latency is added directly to every anonymous page load and API call. Slow or contended DB writes now slow or block authentication, and the panic recovery that the goroutine had is also gone.

findings.title: Device-limit tests miss the update path, MySQL behaviour and the cache bypass
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only covers a new device being rejected. It does not check that an already-registered device under the limit is still updated when the limit is reached, that a device outside the 30-day window is handled, or that re-tagging with unchanged values succeeds on MySQL. There is also no test at the client.go Authenticate level verifying that a limit rejection fails authentication, nor one for the cached-device bypass.

findings.title: New auth.anonymous device_limit option is not documented
findings.body: A new user-facing config key [auth.anonymous] device_limit is read here, but the diff adds no entry to conf/defaults.ini or conf/sample.ini and no docs. Operators have no way to discover that the option exists or what value 0 (unlimited) means.
